verdicts.title: Owner blind read that records its verdict: capture, unblind, report
verdicts.premise_notes: Verified: blind.ts:69 renders the paper 'Preference: A / B / no preference Notes: ___' line; mapping written at blind.ts:77, no reader (blind-check.ts:21 lists it only as a forbidden word); report.ts:424 hard-codes 'Owner blind reading remains pending'; status.md:46 pending; PLAN.md:116 W1 KILL option names planner-as-default. Risk not covered: blind.ts regenerates the planner side by calling today's @mage/director plan()/resolve() on W1 nights; the committed OWNER-READ.html dates from 2026-10-02 and director/core have moved since, so regeneration can silently change what the owner reads. Case 7 pins only the source map, not the morning content. Not on never-re-propose lists.
verdicts.ambition_why: Unblocks the first owner-felt measurement in the evidence system and a pending W1 decision, which is real product leverage.
verdicts.grounding_why: All cited lines hold; the card misses that regenerating the page reruns a planner that has drifted since W1.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Parse/unblind/pageHash cases are sharp; nothing yet catches a regenerated page whose mornings changed.
verdicts.revision: Add acceptance case 8: the inner HTML of the six <article> elements in the regenerated docs/waves/W1-evidence/OWNER-READ.html equals the committed page's six articles byte for byte (the form changes page chrome only, never the mornings); if planner drift makes this fail, inject the form into the committed mornings instead of re-planning.
extra_files_needed: docs/waves/W1-evidence/OWNER-READ.html (regenerated; not in the write set)

verdicts.title: One VR parity harness: shared bout builder, comparator and diff record
verdicts.premise_notes: Verified: vectors.mjs:47-60 createBout deletes state.difficulty and actor.pace and assigns balance, with the '(Request: an unpaced createGames option.)' comment at :54; games.ts:29 createGames options already carry unpaced/balance, :35-36 apply them; conformance.mjs:258 builds games vectors with the 4-arg (paced default) call; VECTORS.md:50 says VR records null. Two comparators (conformance close/firstDiff vs vectors compareNumber with POS_ABS/checkpointMismatch) and two diff shapes confirmed. Not a VR contract change: no vector file or kernel touched; the conformance report's pass set may move because pacing is removed, which aligns PC with VR's rule rather than masking. Builder caution: the conformance adapter must not also start forcing balance:'canonical' unless the vector says so. VECTORS.md:50 describes the hand-strip mechanism and will go stale.
verdicts.ambition_why: Consolidation plus one genuine correctness fix (paced conformance replays); a moderate move.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every anchor, including the pinned-kernel and options claims, checks out.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Case 2's hand-strip equivalence and case 4's per-policy tolerance pins would catch a comparator that silently loosens.

verdicts.title: vr:drift --vectors triage: mask PC-only events, group diffs by cause, flag residue
verdicts.premise_notes: Verified: drift.mjs:99-101 prints P/T then one line per vector; ArenaEvent kinds in types.ts:87 include release/stagger/phase; PC emits release at kernel.ts:216/284, water.ts:79; isDown adapter precedent at conformance.mjs:75-77; rival-plan.ts:38 reads release, so filtering must stay in the exported view; VR checkout present (45 vectors). As written, masking is ON by default and --strict restores the raw view: that is a parity comparison that hides differences by default (policy-loosen per the brief). 'stagger' and 'phase' are not obviously pure representation - they can reflect PC-only rules - so the default mask could hide a real divergence. Shares conformance.mjs/drift.mjs/drift.test.mjs/README with slot A: build after A.
verdicts.ambition_why: Turning 43 diff lines into a cause-grouped work queue before a VR re-pin is a real operator elevation.
verdicts.grounding_why: Event-kind, emit-site and adapter claims all hold on the tree.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Case 2 (a mask may never hide a kind VR emits) and case 7 are good guards; grouping cases are concrete.
verdicts.revision: Keep the strict raw report as the default output of `vr:drift --vectors` (unchanged from today); apply the mask and grouping only under an explicit `--triage` flag whose header prints the raw and masked pass counts side by side, and drop `--strict`.

verdicts.title: One locked spend authority: sessions, every cap and latch clears inside Budget
verdicts.premise_notes: Verified: a13_generate.py:6-10 and a14_generate.py:117-118 check the session cap caller-side, outside .run.lock; a14_session10.py hard-codes 40 and clears the agy stop without providers/.lock; d2_slice.py SESSION_CAP=30 (:28) checked at 271/302/529, literal 450 at 484/530 and check_a14.py:46; d2_slice clear_latch (:150-164) and recover (:185-192) read-modify-write history.json unlocked; wave cap evaluated in providers.generate (:218-220) not Budget.reserve. Tightening, not loosening; no ledger data written. Concerns: the write set rewrites seven closed-wave scripts (a13_*/a14_*/check_a13/14) whose tests (test_a13, test_a14, test_a14_isolation) are not in case 7, and moving checks into reserve can change raised codes (A13_SESSION_CAP / D2S_SESSION_CAP / SESSION10_CAP) that those tests may assert. Shares providers.py with slot B.
verdicts.ambition_why: Making every money cap enforceable only under one lock is the right principal move for a paid pipeline.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every cited cap, literal and unlocked write is on the tree as described.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Cases 2-6 are sharp temp-dir tests; case 7 omits the test modules that cover the migrated closed-wave scripts.
verdicts.revision: Narrow the write set to spend.py, test_spend.py, generate.py, providers.py and d2_slice.py (leave the closed A13/A14 wave scripts and checks untouched), and extend case 7 to `python -m unittest test_providers test_pipeline test_waves test_d2_slice test_a13 test_a14 test_a14_isolation` passing unchanged.
